record.paper_title: I Teoremi di Campbell, Baker, Hausdorff e Dynkin. Storia, Prove, Problemi Aperti.
record.original_question: Let x and y be noncommuting elements and consider the Goldberg presentations of log(exp(x)exp(y)), including the associative word expansion and the commutator expansion obtained from it. What is the optimal domain of absolute convergence for the Goldberg series?

evidence.quote: Il miglior dominio non è ancora stato trovato.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $x$ and $y$ be noncommuting indeterminates, and consider the formal series
$$\log(\exp(x)\exp(y)) = \sum_{n\geq 1}\sum_{w} g_w\, w,$$
where the inner sum runs over all nonempty words $w = z_{i_1} z_{i_2}\cdots z_{i_n}$ in the letters $z_1=x,z_2=y$, and the rational coefficients $g_w \in \mathbb{Q}$ are the Goldberg coefficients (uniquely determined by Goldberg's 1956 explicit formula). Equivalently, by collecting terms one obtains the corresponding commutator (Lie) expansion in nested brackets of $x$ and $y$.

Now let $(\mathcal{A}, \|\cdot\|)$ be a Banach algebra (with submultiplicative norm) and substitute $x,y \in \mathcal{A}$ into the associative-word Goldberg series
$$S(x,y) = \sum_{n\geq 1}\sum_{|w|=n} g_w\, w(x,y).$$

Determine the optimal (largest) domain $D \subseteq \mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{A}$ on which the Goldberg series $S(x,y)$ converges absolutely, i.e., on which
$$\sum_{n\geq 1}\sum_{|w|=n} |g_w|\, \|w(x,y)\| < \infty,$$
and likewise determine the optimal absolute-convergence domain for the associated commutator (Lie) expansion. Goldberg's original argument yields convergence whenever $\|x\|+\|y\|$ is sufficiently small (for instance under the bound $\|x\|+\|y\|<\log 2$, or equivalent restrictions giving radii such as $1/8$ from related estimates), but the sharp/optimal domain is sought.
artifact.status_search_result: The determination of the optimal domain of absolute convergence for the Goldberg/BCH series is widely described in the literature as an open problem. Goldberg (1956) and later works (e.g., Thompson, Blanes–Casas, Michel) provide convergence radii and improved bounds (e.g., 1/8, log 2, or via the Magnus expansion bound 2), but the sharp optimal domain has not been determined. Recent works (2018, 2025, 2026 preprints) continue to refine bounds without settling optimality.

status_evidence.title: Convergence proof for Goldberg's exponential series
status_evidence.snippet: Goldberg's presentation of the formal series for log(e^x e^y) converges when x,y are normed elements in a unit ball, with norm compatible with multiplication.
status_evidence.claim: Known convergence results give explicit but not optimal radii for the Goldberg series.

status_evidence.title: On the convergence and optimization of the Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formula
status_evidence.snippet: The determination of the optimal convergence domain for the BCH series is an open and trying problem; sharp bounds may be obtained via the Magnus expansion.
status_evidence.claim: The optimal convergence domain of the BCH/Goldberg series is open.

status_evidence.title: Local Lie Theory in Quasi-Banach Lie Algebras: Convergence of the BCH Series
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to refine convergence bounds for the BCH series in (quasi-)Banach settings.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues without settling the optimal domain.
